verdict.rationale: Turso documents an official MCP integration that lets an AI agent manage databases and run SQL on the user's behalf. Separately, its auth tokens can be restricted by database, permission level and expiration, and fine-grained permissions control access at table and action level. Nothing shows the MCP tools themselves being scoped or split into read-only versus destructive operations, and the MCP page notes there is no API token to copy, so token scoping is not clearly tied to the agent path. Missing for 10: documented MCP tool-level read-only vs destructive separation, explicit schema-operation tools, a link between token or permission scoping and the MCP agent session, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can run SQL and schema operations through scoped tools that distinguish read-only from destructive actions, so I can safely delegate database work

citations.quote: Connect any MCP-capable AI agent and it can manage your Turso Cloud account — organizations, databases, groups — and run SQL, on your behalf.
Every token can be restricted by database, permission level, and expiration — giving you full control over what each client can and cannot do.
Fine-grained permissions let you control access at the table and action level.
